candidates.name: pyogenic flexor tenosynovitis
support_spans: 1.5-cm painful, fluctuant mass extending from the palmar web space to the A2 pulley of the fourth digit
focal tenderness over the flexor sheath and limited active digit motion
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and examination findings are consistent with an infection of the flexor tendon sheath.

candidates.name: septic arthritis
support_spans: diffuse soft-tissue swelling throughout the palm and into the distal interphalangeal joints of the third and fourth digits
WBC count was 17.5 × 10^9/L
candidates.why: The patient's elevated WBC count and joint swelling suggest a possible infectious process involving the joints.

candidates.name: diabetic foot infection
support_spans: type 2 diabetes (HbA1c 11.2%)
candidates.why: The patient's poorly controlled diabetes increases his risk for infections, particularly in the extremities.

candidates.name: traumatic infection
support_spans: a concrete bench had fallen on the dorsal base of his right fourth digit without skin break
candidates.why: The patient's recent trauma to the hand may have introduced bacteria into the tissue, leading to infection.

candidates.name: osteomyelitis
support_spans: diffuse soft-tissue swelling throughout the palm and into the distal interphalangeal joints of the third and fourth digits
contradict_spans: intact bony anatomy and no fracture or dislocation
candidates.why: While the patient's plain radiographs show no bony involvement, further imaging such as MRI or bone scan may be necessary to rule out osteomyelitis.

candidates.name: cellulitis
support_spans: worsening right hand pain, swelling, and erythema
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms are consistent with cellulitis, and a decisive diagnosis could be made with a combination of clinical examination and laboratory findings.
candidates.axis_node: infection of the skin and soft tissue
